title: I got some great feedback on my AI devlog tool, so here's the actual prototype working
author: Sudden_Network621
selftext:
A few days ago I shared DEVSTORY, a little tool I'm building because I love making games but really don't enjoy creating marketing content for them.

The response was way bigger than I expected. Some people loved the idea, while others had a fair point: **where's the actual output, and how do we know it won't just generate generic AI content?**

So I recorded a walkthrough of the current prototype.

Here's what it does now:

* Nim, my little pixel-art companion, observes your development while you work.
* It collects progress logs, screenshots, artwork and gameplay captures.
* It suggests stories based on what actually happened.
* You can turn those stories into scripts and generate videos.

The goal isn't to create fake inspirational developer stories or another AI content factory.

I want to make games, have my development journey documented automatically, and eventually get short documentary-style videos I can share without spending hours editing.

The video-generation side is still being improved. I'm especially focused on making the stories interesting and keeping the original game footage and artwork intact. Next I will try to integrate video generators like Seedance 2.5 to see how the videos will be generated. 

I'm hoping to get a public prototype into people's hands soon.

**I'd love some feedback on the actual workflow. Is this something you'd use while developing your own game? And what would stop you from using it?**

I'm trying to keep this small and focused rather than turn it into another complicated development tool.

here is the landing page to sign up for the prototype: [https://devstory.base44.app](https://devstory.base44.app)
